subject: [video] WP10 pins the P-mode hang: n2bw_trailing() spins on w->overflow
body:
WP10 -> WP03 (lead cc): the P-mode hang is a one-line non-termination in n2bw_trailing(), pinned with gdb on the current avc/ snapshot (n2avc_mb.c 03:18).

Reproduce (2 frames, P mode; 1 frame returns, 2 hangs):
  clang -std=c11 -O2 -g -Wall -Wextra -pthread -I include avc/*.c avc/test/core/n2avc_cli.c -o n2avc_cli -lm
  gen_yuv.py --pattern gradient --size 176x144 --frames 2 --format i420 --out g.yuv
  ./n2avc_cli --size 176x144 --frames 2 --qp 26 --threads 1 --annexb --in g.yuv --out o.264 --recon r.yuv --stats s.json

gdb after SIGINT:
  Program received signal SIGINT
  n2bw_trailing (w=...) at avc/n2avc_bits.c:73
  73    n2bw_u(w, 1, 0);
  #0 n2bw_trailing
  #1 slice_run (n2avc_enc.c:177)
  #2 n2avc_encode (n2avc_enc.c:478)
  #3 main (n2avc_cli.c:176)

Cause: n2bw_u() returns immediately when w->overflow is set, so once the slice buffer has overflowed and w->nbits != 0, `while (w->nbits) n2bw_u(w, 1, 0);` spins forever. n2bw_align_zero() has the same shape. Suggested fix:
  void n2bw_trailing(n2bw *w) { if (w->overflow) return; ... }
  void n2bw_align_zero(n2bw *w) { if (w->overflow) return; ... }
(or `while (w->nbits && !w->overflow)`).

The overflow itself is the second bug: a 176x144 P slice should never need more than the 1.5*raw+64 KiB slice buffer; frame 1 is 36864 bytes of I_PCM-ish data at QP 26 (raw is 38016), so every macroblock is taking the I_PCM fallback and the P slice then overflows. That matches my earlier observation.

Separate, still open: pick_level returns 31 for 176x144@30/640x480@30 (lead ruled 30 via Table A-1). The 1-frame stream passes every other check_h264 header expectation (profile/constraints/POC/refs/frame_mbs_only/CAVLC/PPS/cropping/reorder/NAL sequence) and its recon is byte-identical to ffmpeg's decode, so the core stream shape is right.
